title: Haryana power employees begin three-day strike against private distribution licence

tea.why: Employees are protesting the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission's decision to grant a private company a 25-year power distribution licence.
tea.want: The unions demand the cancellation of the private licence granted to Eleven Power Private Limited in Gurugram and Nuh.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Approximately 40,000 employees began a three-day strike, causing power and water supply disruptions across the state.

summary: Approximately 40,000 electricity department employees across Haryana began a three-day strike on October 22 to protest the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) granting a 25-year parallel electricity distribution licence to Eleven Power Private Limited. Organised by the Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Front, the strike has led to power supply disruptions in residential and industrial areas of Gurugram and Nuh. The union alleges the move undermines the state-owned Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini stated the government opposes the HERC decision and intends to challenge it before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. He has directed officials to monitor the situation and ensure public services remain functional during the protest. The government has offered to support the unions in legal proceedings against the commission's order.
organizers: Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Front
demands: Cancel the private electricity distribution licence
response: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini stated the government opposes the HERC decision and will challenge it before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. He directed officials to monitor the situation to prevent public inconvenience.

updates.text: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini urged unions to call off the strike and promised to challenge the HERC decision in court.
Approximately 40,000 employees began the three-day strike, resulting in power and water supply disruptions.
